title: Can Machines Help Us Answering Question 16 in Datasheets, and In Turn Reflecting on Inappropriate Content?
measurement_description: The paper focuses on evaluating vision-language models for their ability to semi-automatically detect and document general inappropriate image content (such as offensive, insulting, or threatening imagery) in large computer vision datasets using socio-moral norms. It does not specifically measure or evaluate aspects of religion or faith.
findings: The paper did not specifically evaluate or report findings related to religion. Its primary finding is that pre-trained vision-language models, specifically CLIP using prompt-tuning and MAGMA for caption generation, can effectively identify and document broader dimensions of inappropriate visual content—such as violence, misogyny, and offensive symbols—in large datasets like ImageNet and OpenImages, reducing human labor in datasheet creation.
